edges.description: Mineralocorticoid precursor accumulation in 11 beta-hydroxylase deficiency promotes hypertension.
Cortisol deficiency from impaired CYP17A1 steroidogenesis contributes to adrenal insufficiency.
Mineralocorticoid excess from impaired CYP17A1 steroidogenesis promotes hypertension.
Blocking the shared delta-5 to delta-4 conversion reduces flux into both the glucocorticoid and mineralocorticoid branches.
With cholesterol not reaching the side-chain cleavage step, neither glucocorticoid nor mineralocorticoid synthesis can proceed.
Loss of electron supply reduces CYP21A2 catalysis, producing a partial 21-hydroxylase block without a CYP21A2 variant.

nodes.description: Loss of CYP21A2 21-hydroxylase activity impairs adrenal steroidogenesis, reducing cortisol and, in severe classic disease, aldosterone production. The node is the enzymatic block, not the gene lesion, and it has two inbound routes: a biallelic CYP21A2 variant, which is the usual one and the reason the node is named after the gene, and loss of electron supply from POR, which reduces the same enzyme's catalysis without any CYP21A2 variant. The node name is kept because `kb/node_classes/pathograph_node_classes.txt` cites it as a worked example.

nodes.description: HSD3B2 pathogenic variants reduce the adrenal and gonadal 3-beta-hydroxy-delta5-steroid dehydrogenase that converts delta-5 precursors to their delta-4 counterparts. The step is shared by the glucocorticoid, mineralocorticoid and sex-steroid branches, so unlike the 21- and 11-beta-hydroxylase blocks this one impairs gonadal as well as adrenal steroidogenesis. The placental isozyme HSD3B1 is a different gene and is not implicated.

nodes.description: POR pathogenic variants reduce the NADPH-dependent electron donor that every endoplasmic-reticulum cytochrome P450 requires for catalysis. This is the only lesion in this entry that reaches more than one enzymatic node: the same defect partially disables CYP17A1 and CYP21A2 together, which is why POR deficiency presents as a combined rather than a single-step block, and why it also affects aromatase and hepatic drug-metabolising P450s that lie outside adrenal steroidogenesis altogether.

nodes.description: Loss of the steroidogenic acute regulatory protein removes the delivery of cholesterol to the inner mitochondrial membrane, where side-chain cleavage begins. This node sits above every enzymatic block in this entry: the substrate never reaches the first committed step, so adrenal and gonadal steroid output fails near-completely and unesterified cholesterol accumulates as esters in the adrenal cortex, giving the lipoid form its name.
